WHAT THE CORRECT MECHANISM EXPOSES (the bigger finding -- it is the RESOLVER, not just spot). includePrePost=false is set in equity_path, which is the SAME function the resolver consumes. So the resolver never sees an extended-hours print either. Two compounding biases follow, and BOTH point the same way -- they flatter the instrument:
  (a) INVISIBLE ADVERSE EXCURSION. A stop breached at 02:00Z and recovered before 13:30Z is never observed. The setup stays open and may later book its target. Strictly favourable.
  (b) LOSS TRUNCATION AT GAPS. resolve.py:_walk returns exactly (-1.0,'stop',stop) the moment low<=stop (long), regardless of how far through the stop the bar gapped. Every setup here runs a 1h-240h horizon, so every one of them is held across at least one overnight gap. A name that gaps down 3R through its stop books -1.0R.
Net: reported expectancy is biased UPWARD relative to a real fill.

WHY NOTHING IS BEING CHANGED. Both behaviours sit on the frozen side of the prereg: -1R-at-stop IS the frozen scoring definition and the adverse tie-break is frozen in section 6, and section 7 makes the scoring path and the resolution convention immutable -- an improvement is a NEW instrument, never an edit to this one. A headless supervisor tick is exactly the wrong actor to reopen a frozen scoring rule. A number's distance from zero matters more than its sample size: an instrument that is already negative on charitable accounting is not a near-miss that better fills would rescue.
